items.title: The Elon–Jensen "Understanding"
items.summary: After the SpaceX earnings call on August 4, several pieces started lining up for me in a way that is hard to ignore. Elon didn’t just praise Nvidia hardware, he declared an exclusive commitment to

sourceMetadata.author: @TeslaLarry
sourceMetadata.pageDescription: The Elon–Jensen "Understanding" After the SpaceX earnings call on August 4, several pieces started lining up for me in a way that is hard to ignore. Elon didn’t just praise Nvidia hardware, he declared an exclusive commitment to build on the Vera Rubin architecture for SpaceX AI systems, both on the ground and in orbit. He called it the best AI computer available and spoke of close cooperation and partnership on many levels. That language goes well beyond a standard customer relationship. SpaceX is already co-designing the Starmind AI1 satellite payload with Nvidia. Each of those satellites will carry Rubin GPUs and Vera CPUs for data-center-class compute in orbit. The same rack-scale systems are planned for terrestrial facilities. SpaceX expects a significant share of Nvidia’s GPU output next year. The company is targeting more than 2 gigawatts of compute by the end of 2026 and roughly 10 gigawatts by the end of 2027. Clearly this is more than buying compute in the normal course but a decision to standardize the entire AI infrastructure stack, terrestrial and orbital, on one supplier’s architecture.

items.title: State of Open Models: Summer 2026 Observations

sourceMetadata.pageDescription: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science. Models and datasets on HF hub are growing on a daily basis. Public model repositories grew from 2.43 to 2.96 million over the period, datasets from 711,000 to 1 million, Spaces from 1.00 to 1.44 million. The distribution underneath stays extreme, roughly 85.6% of models have fewer than 200 lifetime downloads, and 1.5% of repositories account for 99.2% of all downloads. Everything below happens inside that shape. There used to be a clear progression path: labs would start by releasing smaller models and gradually work their way toward the top end of the scale. In 2026, several Chinese labs skipped this progression entirely. In almost every month of 2026, the largest and most performant open model from a Chinese lab was larger than anything an American lab released of its own. China's monthly ceiling ran between 754B and 2.78 trillion parameters; America's own ceiling stayed under 130B in five of seven months, the exception being NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Ultra at 561B in May and June, and Inkling from Thinking Machines Lab.

items.summary: When GLM-5.2 helped Hugging Face investigate an incident in which an AI autonomously bypassed its own safeguards, it highlighted a broader shift. AI is becoming part of both cyber offense and cyber

sourceMetadata.author: @Zai_org
sourceMetadata.pageDescription: Preparing GLM-5.3 for Open Release: A Responsible Path to Cyber Defense When GLM-5.2 helped Hugging Face investigate an incident in which an AI autonomously bypassed its own safeguards, it highlighted a broader shift. AI is becoming part of both cyber offense and cyber defense. As powerful cyber capabilities become more accessible, strong defensive capabilities cannot remain limited to a small number of well-resourced organizations. Open-source maintainers, independent researchers, developers, and smaller security teams also need tools that can help them find and fix vulnerabilities before they are exploited. An open world cannot have only open attack surfaces. It must also have an open shield.
